titulo: Three answers at the desk, and the booking carries the rest
subtitulo: Why you came, how many days, where you sleep — short, true, and said in Greek
cena: The queue at passport control in Athens, the officer's eyes already sliding to the next passport in the line.
frasePiso: Answer the question that was asked, then stop. The booking carries everything else.

fatosDatados.afirmacao: Politeness in Greek and in English is described in the research as pulling in opposite directions. Maria Sifianou's comparative work, and the volume on politeness across boundaries she co-edited, describe Greek as oriented to positive politeness — involvement and closeness — and English as oriented to negative politeness — distance and non-imposition. The consequence is documented and symmetrical: the English speaker reads the Greek as abrupt or intrusive, and the Greek reads the English speaker as cold or distant. Both readings are wrong, and each one is produced by the other language's default.
fatosDatados.fonte: A polidez grega é assunto acadêmico e o achado é acionável. Maria Sifianou, «Politeness Phenomena in England and Greece», e Bayraktaroğlu & Sifianou (eds.), «Linguistic Politeness Across Boundaries», John Benjamins, P&BNS 88: o grego é orientado a positive politeness (envolvimento, proximidade) e o inglês a negative politeness (distância, não-imposição). Panorama recente: Languages, 2026, doi:10.3390/languages11050107. Consequência direta, e é documentada e não folclore: o anglófono lê o grego como abrupto ou intrusivo, e o grego lê o anglófono como frio ou distante. As duas leituras são erradas e simétricas.

fatosDatados.afirmacao: Greece figures among the high-proficiency countries in commercial self-selected English indices: EF's 2025 index places it at 592 points, twentieth globally, inside the «High» band, ten points down on the previous year, with speaking the weakest of the four skills at 533. The measure has a caveat EF states itself — respondents are self-selected, online, and skewed towards people already interested in languages — so the index describes Greeks who chose to sit an online test, not the Greek population.
fatosDatados.fonte: EF EPI 2025: Grécia 592, #20 global, banda «High», queda de 10 pontos. Por habilidade: leitura 600, compreensão oral 592, escrita 571, fala 533 — a mais fraca. ⚠️ Ressalva obrigatória, admitida pela própria EF: respondentes autosselecionados, com acesso à internet, enviesados para quem se interessa por idiomas. O EF EPI não mede o inglês da população grega; mede o inglês de gregos que decidiram fazer um teste online. O curso pode dizer «figura entre os países de proficiência alta em índices comerciais de autosseleção» e nunca «X% dos gregos falam inglês».

steps.pt: The desk is three questions, not a Greek exam. Why you came, how many days, where you sleep.
Good morning. What is the purpose of your travel?
steps.acao: Answer the purpose only. Leave the rest of the itinerary out of it.

steps.pt: A short question with no cushioning is the local shape of closeness here, not a sign of impatience.

steps.promptPt: You are here to walk around, eat well and go home again. Say it in four words. Speak now.
steps.pt: Hello. I'm here on holiday.
How many days will you stay?
Use your own number, not the one in this part. The shape of the answer stays exactly this short.

steps.promptPt: Give the length of the stay and nothing else. Two words. Speak now.
steps.pt: Ten days.
Where will you be staying?
steps.acao: Name the town and the kind of place. Stop there.

steps.pt: Not the story of how you found the place. Town, kind of place, full stop.

steps.promptPt: Say where you sleep, briefly — the town and the kind of place. Speak now.
steps.pt: In Athens, in a hotel.
Do you have the booking?

steps.promptPt: Hand over the offline copy you saved last night, and let the document do the talking. Speak now.
steps.pt: Yes, here you are.
Ορίστε is the whole sentence. Three syllables and an open hand outrun any paragraph you could build.
If it went past you, say so once. Συγγνώμη opens the repair and no desk minds hearing it.

steps.promptPt: It went past you too fast. Say so cleanly, without apologising twice. Speak now.
steps.pt: Sorry, I didn't understand.

steps.promptPt: The question came back at the same speed as the first time. Ask for the one thing that would fix it. Speak now.
steps.pt: Sorry, more slowly?
Μόνος μου if you are a man, μόνη μου if you are a woman. One letter, and it is the only thing that moves.

steps.promptPt: Nobody is with you on this trip. Say it in three words, in the form that matches you. Speak now.
steps.pt: I'm travelling alone. (a man speaking — a woman says μόνη μου)

steps.promptPt: They ask whether Athens is the whole trip. Answer truthfully and briefly. Speak now.
steps.pt: Then I'm going to Santorini.
Some officers switch to English and some do not. The three Greek answers work either way.
All right. Enjoy your stay.

steps.promptPt: Four words, take the passport, walk. Speak now.
steps.pt: Thank you. Have a good day.

steps.es: Ήρθα για διακοπές. Δέκα μέρες. Στην Αθήνα, σε ξενοδοχείο. Ναι, ορίστε.
steps.pinyin: IR-tha ya dhia-ko-PES. DHE-ka ME-res. stin a-THI-na, se kse-no-dho-KHI-o. ne, o-RI-ste
steps.pt: Shadow the three answers, with a clean stop after each one.
steps.tts: Ήρθα για διακοπές. Δέκα μέρες. Στην Αθήνα, σε ξενοδοχείο. Ναι, ορίστε.

steps.pt: B05 done. Purpose, days, where you sleep, ορίστε. Short is not evasive — short means the answer matched.

aprofundar.titulo: The desk is a matching task

secoes.corpo: Never repeat this part's ten days when your own ticket says something else. Swap the number for the truth; the sentence stays the same length and the same shape, and δέκα is the only word in it that changes.

Purpose, length and address are three separate answers, not one speech. Stacking all three before you were asked for them is the most common way a thirty-second exchange turns into a three-minute one — and it is the habit visitors bring with them, not something the desk provokes.

exemplos.pt: How many days will you stay?

secoes.titulo: Ορίστε, and the paper doing the talking
secoes.corpo: Ορίστε is one of the most useful words in the language and it has three jobs: here you are, as you hand something over; go ahead, when someone approaches you; and sorry, what?, said with a rising tone. At a desk it is the first of the three, and it moves the exchange off your memory and onto your evidence.

secoes.titulo: The word that changes with who is speaking
secoes.corpo: Μόνος μου and μόνη μου are the same sentence said by a man and by a woman. Greek does this in a lot of places, and here it is a single letter at the end. Learn the one that is yours and never think about the other again.

secoes.titulo: The rules move, so check them close to departure
secoes.corpo: This part teaches the conversation at the desk, not the paperwork behind it. Entry requirements change, and a course file is the wrong place to read them from — check the official source for your own passport shortly before you fly.

permissao: You are allowed to answer in three words and stop. A short true answer is not evasive; over-explaining, filling the pause with detail nobody asked for, or trying to sound friendlier than the question calls for is what actually slows a border desk down — and you are permitted to simply not do it.
espelho: Anyone who has over-answered an officer at home, volunteering a whole itinerary to a question about one night, knows the instinct this part corrects. It is not a Greek phenomenon — it is the nervous habit of filling a silence with more words than the question needed, and it reads identically on either side of any border.

fichasCulturais.sinal: The question arrives bare — no softening, no please, no smile in front of it — and you hear it as displeasure aimed at you.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: Something about me is a problem, or he has decided he does not like the look of my passport.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: The comparative research on politeness describes Greek as oriented to involvement and closeness and English as oriented to distance and non-imposition. The softening layer an English speaker expects in front of a question is doing work that Greek does elsewhere, so its absence carries no message at all. The mirror image is documented too: the English speaker's padding reads back as cold.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Answer the content of the question at the same directness it was asked, and resist the urge to add cushioning that would only make the exchange longer.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: The exchange runs at the rhythm the desk is already set up for, and you stop spending the queue rereading a tone that was never about you.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: This describes an orientation between two languages, not a prediction about a particular person. A passport desk is also a scripted setting where brevity is procedure, and a tired officer at the end of a shift is sometimes just a tired officer.

fichasCulturais.sinal: The officer asks one short question and you hear yourself adding an explanation nobody requested — why this trip, what you did last time, how much you have been looking forward to it.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: More detail sounds open and friendly, and proves I have nothing to hide.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: The desk is working through a queue of short matched answers. A reply that runs past the question it answered reads as material to check rather than as warmth, and the line behind you is part of the officer's afternoon.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Answer only the payload of the question you were actually asked, then stop and wait for the next one.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You are through faster rather than slower, and the three sentences you practised are enough for the whole desk.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not when the officer asks a compound question or explicitly invites more. Then answering everything they asked is the match, and a clipped reply is the mismatch.
